Data.subject: Research and Development (R&D)
Data.title: Research And Development Expenditure By Type Of Costs And Institutional Sector, Annual
Data.datasource: AGENCY FOR SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY AND RESEARCH
Data.footnote: Data on research and development (R&D) in Singapore are collected through the National Survey of Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE), conducted on an annual basis by the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR).  The institutional sectors in the RIE Survey are broadly split into three sectors, namely (a) 'Private sector' comprises all business enterprises, excluding institutions of higher learning; (b) 'Government sector' comprises all government organisations, including government ministries, statutory boards & public research institutes and excluding institutes of higher learning; and (c) 'Institutes of Higher Learning' comprises institutions of higher learning, including the universities and polytechnics.

row.footnote: Prior to 2000, postgraduate research students (at the master degree and PhD levels) were not collected as R&D manpower.  For 2000, figures refer to full-time and part-time postgraduate research students.  From 2001 onwards, figures refer to only full-time postgraduate research students.

Postgraduate research students doing research work with Public Research Institutes are reported under Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) since they are matriculated with the IHLs.  Prior to 2000, postgraduate research students (at the master degree and PhD levels) were not collected as R&D manpower.  For 2000, figures refer to full-time and part-time postgraduate research students.  From 2001 onwards, figures refer to only full-time postgraduate research students.
With effect from the release of 2022 publication, public research entities have been subsumed under the Government Sector for conceptual alignment with OECD.

Data only collected for public research institutes and from 2020 onwards.  Refers to postgraduate research students doing research work with Public Research Institutes but matriculated with overseas Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs).  Those matriculate with local IHLs are reported under the category for IHLs.
